status: Chain-free sim traces (M6.1 plan commit A) for the derived-metrics property harness (spec requirement R3): deposit/redemption/epoch events from the production planners, never captured from a live chain.
regeneration_command: cd contracts && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.24.5 cargo run --release --bin simulate -- --seed <seed> --scenarios 1 --epochs 48 --report-secs 0 --trace-out ../packages/fixtures/fixtures/sim-traces

conventions.actors: Deposits and redemption requests are tagged (round-robin, no rng draw) with one of 3 synthetic addresses (user-0, user-1, user-2) for trace attribution; the sim otherwise models a single pooled depositor. The tag is metadata only: every pooled entry, amount, and RNG draw is identical to an untraced run of the same seed (see contracts/src/sim.rs tests trace_per_actor_totals_match_pooled_stats and tracing_never_changes_economics).
conventions.epoch_index: 1-based, matching the contract's EPOCH_INDEX (first settled epoch = 1). An event's epoch_index is the count of epochs already settled at the moment the event occurred (0 before the first epoch settles).
conventions.amounts: shares and nhash are decimal strings (u128 base units). nhash is "0" on swap_out_request and redemption_refund, which carry no nhash leg (mirrors TransactionRow in packages/api-types/src/rows.ts).
conventions.stats_derivation: Each trace's stats below are counted directly from that file's events array (swap_in / swap_out_request / redemption_payout / redemption_refund), not copied from the simulate binary's own report line. swap_out_request may exceed redemption_payout + redemption_refund by the count still pending (not yet due) when the scenario's epoch budget ran out; slashes and write_downs come from the binary's report line (not separately recorded as trace events).

traces.notes: Moderate economy with heavy redelegation churn; includes redemption refunds.
High-deposit, high-TVL economy with frequent slashing but no write-down epoch in this window; includes redemption refunds.
REQUIRED coverage scenario: includes both redemption refunds and a slash write-down (a TVV step-down not fully explained by redemption payouts alone).
High-churn economy (heaviest redelegation volume of the set) with slashing but no refunds or write-downs in this window.
Quiet-ish baseline economy: zero slashes, one refund, for contrast against the more heavily stressed scenarios above.
